prompt: In a workflow, the `deploy` job has `needs: [build, test]`. What does this actually cause?
choices: deploy runs before build and test, to warm up the environment
deploy runs in parallel with build and test to save time
deploy waits until both build and test complete successfully before it starts
deploy only runs if build and test are both skipped

prompt: Which trigger block fires when someone pushes a tag like v1.2.0, but not on ordinary commits to main?
choices: on: push: branches: [main]
on: pull_request: branches: [main]
on: push: tags: ['v*']
on: push: branches: ['v*']

prompt: A deploy step accidentally echoes an environment variable that was set from a repository secret. Why doesn't the real value show up in the GitHub Actions log?
choices: GitHub scans raw log output and replaces any text matching a registered secret's value with ***
Secrets are encrypted in the log and only decrypted when you view it in a browser you're logged into
run: steps are not allowed to read environment variables derived from secrets
The secret is deleted from memory before any run step can execute

prompt: Following the "never commit state" principle, where should a database password used during a CI deploy step actually live?
choices: Hardcoded directly in the workflow YAML file for simplicity
In a .env file committed to the repo and loaded with a dotenv library
In the repository's Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions, referenced as ${{ secrets.NAME }}
In a comment directly above the deploy step so reviewers can verify it

prompt: A cache step uses key: ${{ runner.os }}-npm-${{ hashFiles('**/package-lock.json') }}. This cache will miss (forcing a fresh dependency install) primarily when:
choices: The workflow runs on a different calendar day than the last run
package-lock.json changes, which changes the computed hash
The job is named deploy instead of build
More than 10 jobs are defined in the same workflow file

prompt: What is the actual difference between `uses:` and `run:` inside a job's steps list?
choices: uses: executes arbitrary shell commands; run: references a reusable packaged Action
uses: references a reusable, versioned Action; run: executes a literal shell command on the runner
They are interchangeable syntax for the same behavior
uses: only works with actions/checkout; run: only works for running tests

prompt: A workflow triggered by `pull_request` from a fork branch typically cannot access the base repository's secrets. Why?
choices: Fork-hosted runners have no network access to GitHub's secret store
Secrets cost extra for runs triggered from forks
It prevents a malicious PR from modifying workflow code in the fork to exfiltrate secrets it shouldn't have
pull_request events don't support environment variables at all

prompt: A repo has both `on: push: branches: [main]` and `on: pull_request: branches: [main]` workflows. When a PR is merged into main, both workflows end up running at different points. Why is this not a bug?
choices: pull_request fired earlier to validate the proposed merge preview before landing; push fired separately for the merge commit that actually landed on main — two distinct, legitimate events
It is a known bug in GitHub Actions that always double-runs on merge
pull_request workflows never actually execute, only push workflows do
push triggers only fire on tag pushes, never on branch commits
